nodes.title: tip-split: vision
nodes.text:
A tiny command-line tool that splits a restaurant bill, plus tip, fairly between people, so nobody argues about the last cent.

First user moment: `tipsplit 100.00 3 --tip 15` prints three lines that add up to exactly $115.00, with the extra cent given to the first person.

Out of scope: currencies other than dollars; uneven or weighted splits; saving history.

nodes.title: Money is integer cents everywhere
nodes.text: tip-split amounts are integer cents everywhere; never floats (D1)

nodes.title: Fair split
nodes.text: Shares differ by at most one cent. Leftover cents go to the first people in order.

nodes.title: Tip rounding
nodes.text: The tip is a whole-number percentage from 0 to 100, rounded half up to the cent.

nodes.title: Input forms
nodes.text: Amounts like `12`, `12.3`, `12.34` and `$12.34` are accepted. Negative amounts, more than two decimals and garbage are rejected.

nodes.title: Error contract
nodes.text: Invalid input prints a one-line error to stderr and exits with code 2. Success exits with 0.

nodes.title: Money core
nodes.text: Parse dollar amounts and split the tipped total fairly using integer cents.

nodes.title: Command line
nodes.text: Accept a total, people and optional tip percentage; print each person's share.

nodes.title: Split a bill fairly
nodes.text: As a diner, I want shares that sum to the exact tipped total and differ by at most one cent.

nodes.title: Read shares from the terminal
nodes.text: As a diner, I want a simple command that prints dollar amounts for each person and clear errors for invalid inputs.

nodes.title: Parse amounts (D1, D4)
nodes.text: `parse_amount(text) -> int` returns cents: `"12.34"` → 1234, `"$12"` → 1200 and `"12.3"` → 1230. It raises `ValueError` for negative amounts, more than two decimals, or garbage.

nodes.title: Fair tipped shares (D2, D3)
nodes.text: `split(total_cents, people, tip_percent=0) -> list[int]` returns `people` shares that sum to the total plus the tip, rounded half up. Shares differ by at most 1 cent, and leftover cents go to the first people.

nodes.title: Reject invalid split inputs
nodes.text: `split` raises `ValueError` when `people < 1` or when `tip_percent` is not between 0 and 100.

nodes.title: Format cents and shares (D1)
nodes.text: `format_cents(cents) -> str` returns `"$12.34"`-style text. `format_shares(shares) -> list[str]` returns lines in the form `"Person 1: $38.34"`.

nodes.title: Command-line success and error contract (D5)
nodes.text: `main(argv) -> int` parses `TOTAL PEOPLE [--tip PCT]` and prints one line per person to stdout. It returns 0 on success. `cli.py` imports `from tipsplit.money import parse_amount, split` into its own namespace and calls those names, so Bead B's tests can stand in for Bead A. On invalid input it prints a one-line error to stderr and returns 2.

nodes.title: Integrated restaurant bill
nodes.text:
`main(["100.00", "3", "--tip", "15"])` prints exactly:

- `Person 1: $38.34`
- `Person 2: $38.33`
- `Person 3: $38.33`

They sum to $115.00. `tests/test_end_to_end.py` passes on the integrated result.

nodes.title: Bead A: money core
nodes.text: Implement the public money functions; record the D1 lesson after validation.

nodes.title: Bead B: command line
nodes.text: Implement the command line; depend on A's public functions at integration time only.

nodes.title: Money unit proof
nodes.text: Verify parsing, fair splitting and rejected split inputs.

nodes.title: Command-line unit proof
nodes.text: Verify formatting, success and errors with money functions stood in for.

nodes.title: Integrated bill proof
nodes.text: Run the real integrated command line and verify the three shares sum to $115.00.
